_about: Maps the ITU AI Readiness framework dimensions to actual evidence from
the project corpus. Evidence is drawn only from ingested sources.
- No quantitative readiness scores are assigned.
- No unsupported maturity levels are claimed.
- No compliance claims are made that the evidence does not support.
- Where evidence is unavailable in the ingested corpus, the dimension
is explicitly marked as 'evidence unavailable in corpus'.
- All source citations reference actual ingested documents with their
document IDs, chunk IDs, and sections as recorded in the KB.
ITU AI Readiness Assessment reference framework dimensions are based on
publicly available ITU resources. This mapping is for project evidence
purposes only and does not constitute a formal ITU readiness assessment.
scope: 5G network deployment and AI-enabled telecommunications governance
methodology_disclaimer: This is an evidence mapping, not a formal ITU AI Readiness Assessment. No readiness score or maturity level is assigned. Formal assessment requires qualified evaluators and comprehensive data beyond this corpus.

dimensions.description: National AI strategy, digital transformation plans, government commitment to AI governance.

evidence_items.claim: India has a National Digital Communications Policy (2018) that sets connectivity and digital infrastructure goals including 5G.
evidence_items.caveat: Policy document, not legally binding legislation. Specific 5G-readiness targets must be verified against current DoT publications.

evidence_items.claim: TRAI has issued recommendations on AI and Big Data for the telecommunications sector (July 2023), signalling regulatory attention to AI-enabled 5G.
evidence_items.source_title: TRAI Recommendations on Leveraging AI and Big Data in Telecommunication Sector
evidence_items.caveat: Recommendations to Government, not enacted law. The degree of Government uptake is not confirmed in the ingested corpus.

evidence_unavailable: IndiaAI Mission 2024 documentation not ingested
NITI Aayog National Strategy for AI (2018) not ingested
Specific AI-readiness targets or KPIs from Government sources not in corpus

dimensions.description: Telecommunications infrastructure quality, 5G deployment status, connectivity.

evidence_items.claim: India has a national telecommunications regulatory framework under the Telecommunications Act 2023, which provides the legal basis for 5G spectrum assignment and authorisation.
evidence_items.caveat: The Act establishes the regulatory framework; it does not contain deployment statistics or infrastructure readiness data.

evidence_unavailable: 5G deployment coverage or penetration statistics not in corpus
Spectrum auction outcomes not in corpus
Infrastructure quality metrics not in corpus

dimensions.description: Existence and quality of laws governing AI, data protection, cybersecurity, and digital services.

evidence_items.claim: India enacted the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023), establishing a personal data protection framework including breach notification obligations.
evidence_items.source_title: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
evidence_items.caveat: Commencement of individual provisions notified separately and not verified. Effective status: not verified.

evidence_items.claim: India enacted the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)) implementing the DPDP Act, including breach intimation procedures.
evidence_items.caveat: Phase-wise commencement; phase applicability per rule not checked.

evidence_items.claim: India enacted the Telecommunications (Telecom Cyber Security) Rules 2024 (G.S.R. 720(E)) requiring mandatory security incident reporting within 6 hours.
evidence_items.caveat: Effective status not verified; amendments not checked.

evidence_items.claim: India established CERT-In with mandatory incident reporting obligations for service providers under IT Act 2000 section 70B (Directions, April 2022).
evidence_items.source_title: CERT-In Directions under s.70B of IT Act 2000
evidence_items.caveat: A later clarification notice (27 June 2022) exists and was not ingested.

evidence_items.claim: India enacted the Telecommunications Act 2023, replacing the Indian Telegraph Act 1885 and establishing a modern telecommunications legal framework.
evidence_items.caveat: Commencement of individual sections notified separately and not verified.

evidence_unavailable: IT Act 2000 not separately ingested (parent of CERT-In Directions)
NCIIPC Rules 2013 NOT INGESTED (CII designation criteria unavailable)
AI-specific regulatory framework: no dedicated AI liability or AI governance Act in corpus

dimensions.description: Policies, guidelines, and frameworks ensuring ethical, fair, and trustworthy deployment of AI systems.

evidence_items.claim: TRAI (2023) recommended algorithmic accountability and transparency frameworks for AI use in telecommunications, indicating regulatory attention to AI ethics in telecom.
evidence_items.source_title: TRAI Recommendations on Leveraging AI and Big Data in Telecommunication Sector
evidence_items.caveat: Recommendations only, not enacted. Specific algorithmic accountability obligations do not yet have statutory force based on the ingested corpus.

evidence_unavailable: No dedicated AI ethics policy or AI governance Act in ingested corpus
IndiaAI Mission ethical AI framework not ingested
MeitY AI governance papers not ingested

dimensions.description: National cybersecurity posture, incident response capabilities, and security standards compliance.

evidence_items.claim: India established NCIIPC as the national body for critical information infrastructure protection and CERT-In for cyber incident response, as evidenced in the National Cyber Security Policy 2013.
evidence_items.caveat: 2013 policy document; institutional developments since 2013 are not reflected in this source alone.

evidence_items.claim: India's Telecom Cyber Security Rules 2024 mandate security measures, audits, and incident reporting for telecom entities, aligned with international practice.
evidence_items.section: Rule 4 (security measures), Rule 7 (incident reporting), Rule 8 (security audit)

evidence_unavailable: NCIIPC Rules 2013 NOT INGESTED — CII protection capabilities not confirmable from corpus
Actual CERT-In capacity or incident statistics not in corpus
Penetration testing or red-team capabilities not addressed in corpus

dimensions.description: Data governance frameworks, open data policies, and data-sharing mechanisms.

evidence_items.claim: The DPDP Act 2023 establishes data-fiduciary obligations for personal data processing in India, including a breach notification framework.
evidence_items.source_title: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
evidence_items.caveat: Commencement not verified; does not address open data or non-personal data governance.

evidence_items.claim: TRAI (2023) recommended data-sharing frameworks and open data policies for AI in telecom, indicating regulatory direction on data governance.
evidence_items.source_title: TRAI Recommendations on Leveraging AI and Big Data in Telecommunication Sector

evidence_unavailable: Non-Personal Data Governance Framework not ingested
Open government data policy not in corpus
Data localisation obligations: DPDP Rules 2025 contain localisation provisions but their commencement is not verified

dimensions.description: R&D investment, academic capacity, and innovation support for AI and 5G.
evidence_unavailable: R&D investment data not in corpus
Academic capacity indicators not in corpus
Innovation policy instruments not ingested

dimensions.description: Workforce readiness, training programmes, and human capital for AI and 5G.
evidence_unavailable: Skills-gap assessment data not in corpus

dimensions.description: Participation in international standards bodies, bilateral/multilateral AI and telecom agreements.

evidence_items.claim: India participates in ITU standardisation through ITU membership; the ingested ITU-T Y.3172 standard (2019) provides the architectural framework that this project maps to.
evidence_items.caveat: [REFERENCE ONLY — not Indian law]. Confirms ITU-T framework exists; does not confirm India's specific participation or commitment.

evidence_unavailable: Bilateral AI or telecom agreements not in corpus
India's formal ITU positions or contributions not in corpus
3GPP membership contribution details not in corpus

overall_evidence_summary.key_gap_in_evidence: NCIIPC Rules 2013 not ingested — this is the single most significant gap for CII protection and cybersecurity readiness evidence.
overall_evidence_summary.no_readiness_score_assigned: true — quantitative scores require comprehensive assessment beyond the scope of this corpus mapping.
overall_evidence_summary.no_maturity_level_claimed: true — maturity levels are not assigned without formal assessment methodology and complete evidence.
